summary: Defines an Instant Messaging identity KeyPurposeId for the Extended Key Usage extension in X.509 v3 certificates, adding to the purposes listed in RFC 5280.

plainLanguage.summary: A certificate can say what it may be used for. This adds a purpose label for proving who you are in chat messaging.

questions: what is an extended key usage for instant messaging
why do im certificates need a key purpose
subtitle: A certificate key purpose that marks a certificate as meant for proving instant messaging identity.

tldr.problem: Organizations may be unwilling to issue instant messaging client certificates with a general purpose such as id-kp-clientAuth, because of the risk of cross-protocol attacks.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines the KeyPurposeId id-kp-imUri, object identifier { id-kp 40 }, for the Extended Key Usage extension of X.509 v3 certificates.
tldr.outcome: Certificates can be limited to IM identity use. Issuers SHOULD NOT combine it with id-kp-clientAuth or id-kp-serverAuth.

today: RFC 9734 is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Why an IM Key Purpose
sections.content:
Instant messaging systems using Messaging Layer Security (RFC 9420) can use per-client identity certificates. A subjectAltName in such a certificate can be an IM URI or an XMPP URI. Organizations may be unwilling to issue these certificates with a general KeyPurposeId like id-kp-serverAuth or id-kp-clientAuth, because the certificates could be abused in a cross-protocol attack.

The credentials are expected to be heavily used in the More Instant Messaging Interoperability (MIMI) Working Group.
sections.plainLanguage: A key that opens every door is risky. A key marked only for the chat room is safer to hand out.

sections.title: The id-kp-imUri Key Purpose
sections.content:
The RFC defines the KeyPurposeId id-kp-imUri, which may be included in certificates used to prove the identity of an IM client. It sits under the PKIX key purpose arc as id-kp-imUri OBJECT IDENTIFIER ::= { id-kp 40 }. The issuer MAY mark the Extended Key Usage extension as either critical or non-critical.

Appendix A gives an ASN.1 module named IM-EKU that contains this definition.
sections.plainLanguage: It is a new purpose sticker, number 40 on the official list, saying this certificate is for chat identity.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security considerations of RFC 5280 apply. The RFC says the new purpose does not introduce new security risks and instead reduces existing ones, by identifying certificates generated to sign IM identity credentials.

Issuers SHOULD NOT set id-kp-imUri together with id-kp-clientAuth or id-kp-serverAuth, since that would defeat the added specificity.
sections.plainLanguage: Do not put the chat sticker and the open-every-door sticker on the same key, or the chat sticker means nothing.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA registered decimal 40, id-kp-imUri, in the "SMI Security for PKIX Extended Key Purpose" registry (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3). It also registered decimal 113, id-mod-im-eku, in the "SMI Security for PKIX Module Identifier" registry (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.0) for the ASN.1 module.
sections.plainLanguage: The official list of stickers now includes this one, so everyone uses the same number for it.
